name: McColley's Finale Philodendron
description: Philodendron 'McColley's Finale' is a patented self-heading hybrid Philodendron selected from complex hybrid seedlings of unknown parentage in the Orlando, Florida breeding programme associated with Robert H. McColley, Cora McColley, and Dr Howard N. Miller (USPP12144P2). New leaves emerge rich chestnut-red to copper-orange, then deepen through bronze tones before maturing to glossy dark green, keeping the crown colourful. The plant forms a compact, dense rosette from a short central stem rather than climbing, typically reaching about 45–90 cm tall and wide indoors. It prefers bright filtered light, warm temperatures, and an airy, well-draining aroid mix. Like other Philodendron, all parts contain calcium oxalate crystals and are toxic if ingested.
careTips: Provide bright, indirect light to keep new leaves vividly coloured; avoid harsh midday sun that can scorch glossy young foliage
Water when the top 3–4 cm of mix feels dry; keep evenly moist but never soggy around the crown
Use an airy, well-draining aroid mix (bark, perlite/pumice, peat or coco) to protect thick roots from rot
Aim for humidity around 50–60% or higher; steadier humidity helps new leaves expand cleanly
Keep temperatures about 18–27 °C (65–80 °F); protect from cold drafts below ~15 °C
Wipe leaves occasionally and check for spider mites, scale, and mealybugs
Propagate from crown offshoots or stem cuttings with a node when the plant is mature enough to divide
Toxic if ingested – keep away from pets and children
